prompts.display_text: Pin the Hyde Park Chapel in London, dedicated by David O. McKay in 1961.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Hyde Park Chapel on Exhibition Road in South Kensington, London, the Church's landmark meetinghouse dedicated by David O. McKay in 1961.
prompts.citation: Wikipedia and Church News; Wikidata and OpenStreetMap for the location, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The Hyde Park Chapel stands on Exhibition Road in South Kensington, London, by the museums. President David O. McKay asked the British Mission to find a central London site; the building, with its gold-leaf spire and a dalle de verre stained-glass window, took 16 months to build and was dedicated by President McKay on 26 February 1961. It houses a chapel, a visitors' center and a family history center, and was refurbished and rededicated in 1995.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a named local convert led a branch as its president before 1900.
prompts.text_original: A country where a local convert was named as a branch president before 1900.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Early branches abroad were usually led by local converts. The chronologies name some of them: John Skerry in Halifax (1843), Hans Peter Jensen in Aalborg (1850), Carl J. E. Fjeld in Christiania (1853), Gudmundur Gudmundsson in Iceland (1853), Timotheus Mets in Rotterdam (1863), Hare Te Katera in New Zealand (1883) and Frederick Pieper in Antwerp (1891).

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: With the organization of the Halifax Branch in 1843, John Skerry became the first in Canada to be ordained an elder and serve as branch president.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: A branch was organized at Aalborg on November 25, 1850, with Hans Peter Jensen as branch president.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Timotheus Mets, the first Dutch branch president, led the Rotterdam Branch from November 1, 1863.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: The Christiania Branch was organized with nine members in 1853, with Carl J. E. Fjeld as its president.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: The first Maori branch was organized at Waotu in 1883 with Hare Te Katera as president.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: A branch was created in Antwerp before January 1891 with Frederick Pieper as president.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: The first branch in Iceland was organized in 1853 with Gudmundur Gudmundsson as president.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose government banned the Church or expelled its missionaries during the 1900s.
prompts.text_original: A country whose government banned Church activity or expelled its missionaries in the 20th century.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Governments shut the Church out more than once in the 20th century: Hungary outlawed meetings around 1901, Mexico expelled foreign clergy in 1926, Communist Czechoslovakia banned the Church in 1950, Ghana locked meetinghouses in 1989, and Liberia's civil war closed its mission in 1991.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: On April 6, 1950, Communist officials banned the Church from all public activity and expelled all foreign missionaries; no foreign missionaries served until 1989.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: In June 1989 Ghana's government, acting on misinformation, banned the Church; foreign missionaries were deported, meetinghouses locked and public meetings prohibited until 1990.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: During the Cristero Rebellion in 1926 all foreign clergy and missionaries were expelled from Mexico, leaving local leaders to carry on.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: As part of Czechoslovakia, Slovakia saw the Church banned from public activity and all foreign missionaries expelled on April 6, 1950.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Around 1901 missionaries renewed work in Hungary although they were legally banned from holding Church meetings.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: In July 1990 Liberian missionaries fled the civil war to Sierra Leone, and in February 1991 the Liberia Monrovia Mission was discontinued.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where an early branch of the Church began with fewer than 20 members, before 1880.
prompts.text_original: A country where an early branch was organized with fewer than 20 members, before 1880.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The chronologies record the size of some founding branches: 12 members in Glasgow (1840), 12 in Hamburg (1852), 18 at Risor and 9 in Christiania (1852-53), 15 in Amsterdam (1862) and 8 in the Westman Islands (1874).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: The Hamburg Branch was organized on August 1, 1852, consisting of 12 members.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: A branch was organized in Glasgow with 12 members in August 1840.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Amsterdam Branch was organized in 1862 with 15 members.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: The first branch in Norway was created at Risor in 1852 with 18 members; the Christiania Branch followed in 1853 with nine.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: A new branch with eight members was organized in the Westman Islands on May 29, 1874.
